page: Microsoft Azure DC48es_v6 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon TDX processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. System memory totals 192.0 GB, representing a 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 (foundation, VNNI, and BF16) and AMX (tile and int8), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached remote storage volumes for state persistence. In performance benchmarking, the instance shows upper-quartile computational capability, recording strong scores in Geekbench multi-core execution (18106.0) and PassMark CPU evaluation (62237.33). Extended instruction tests and image processing benchmarks fall into the highest tiers, while memory throughput metrics and Redis SET benchmarks (54.85 million operations per second) demonstrate median performance.

Resource allocation provides high compute density per physical socket, offering balanced throughput for non-accelerated compute loads. The absence of local solid-state drives necessitates external storage configuration for I/O-intensive workloads. The platform is well matched for software build farms, relational databases, continuous integration pipelines, and matrix-intensive backend data processing.
